course_description:
This course extends Plant Science from foundational knowledge to an advanced experience in a plant science research topic of choice. Students undertaking this course will be experiencing, in a team environment, cutting edge research and the questions and techniques that lead to innovation. Students in BIOL2903 explore a literature-based topic that is guided by an expert mentor, evaluated and communicated to peers and experts by the student.

Plants are integral to life on our planet. They provide oxygen, habitat, food, energy and materials. The focus on plants and their roles in the future bioeconomy is intensifying as countries are transitioning to become carbon neutral. Course participants will dive deep into the current knowledge of plant biology - spanning from evolution, ecology, conservation, agriculture to biotechnology. Topics include plant biodiversity and function, adaptation to environments, interactions with beneficial and pathogenic organisms, and improvement for human uses. The wide-ranging roles and uses of plants are explored with view of food and a sustainable future. Participants experience hands-on activities, from interactive lectures and discussions, to workshops, practicals and networking with world-class plant biologists.

Plants have shaped life on Earth for over 400 million years and understanding them has never been more urgent. With hundreds of thousands of species yet to be fully understood, there has never been a more exciting time to discover the plant kingdom and uncover the vital roles plants play in every ecosystem on Earth. Plant biologists are rising to the planet's greatest challenges, from protecting threatened species and reversing habitat loss, to developing the crops and biomaterials that will define our future.

In BIOL2903, you'll go beyond the textbook. You'll investigate how plants function at a molecular and ecological level, how they sense and respond to their environment, and how science is harnessing their potential to address global challenges in food, health, and sustainability.

This course is built around hands-on learning. Weekly practicals take you from plant identification and anatomy to sterile lab technique, molecular biology, and biotechnology. You'll design and conduct your own experiments, analyse real data, and communicate your findings. These skills are directly transferable to careers in ecology, environmental science, agriculture, conservation biology, plant pathology, horticulture, forestry, botanical research, science communication, biosecurity, and food systems and sustainability.

Teaching is delivered by world-class plant biologists who combine interactive lectures with inquiry-based and student-centered learning.

What students say:

"My favourite course at UQ so far! A great introduction to all aspects of plant science and fungal biology. The pracs were very hands-on and lots of fun!"

"The lecturers encourage real thinking ... I am now doing a third-year plant subject. It made me realise that a good knowledge of plant biology is a vital tool for problem-solving environmental issues."

At the School of Agriculture and Food Sustainability, we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge-sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold students and staff accountable for actively contributing to establishing a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and against UQ Policy, and will not be tolerated. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain plant structure and function in context of evolution and adaptation to diverse environments
As an individual or part of a student team design and/or perform experiments addressing well-defined questions in plant biology
